claim: Lung adenocarcinoma is the most common form of lung cancer.
source: Lung adenocarcinoma is the most common form of lung cancer, the leading cause of cancer-related death worldwide.
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction section of the manuscript.

claim: Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer-related death worldwide.
source: Lung adenocarcinoma is the most common form of lung cancer, the leading cause of cancer-related death worldwide.
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction section of the manuscript.

claim: Most lung adenocarcinoma patients require systemic chemotherapy because the disease is typically diagnosed late.
source: Lung adenocarcinoma is typically diagnosed late, meaning that most patients require systemic chemotherapy (Chen et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Chen et al., 2014.

claim: Resistance to targeted therapies emerges in EGFR, ALK or ROS mutant tumours.
source: Platinum-based chemotherapy is likely to remain an important treatment modality for these patients due to the emergence of resistance to targeted therapies in EGFR, ALK or ROS mutant tumours (Lindeman et al., 2018), and the fact that most patients do not respond to single agent immunotherapy (Kim et al., 2019; Doroshow et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Lindeman et al., 2018.

claim: Most patients do not respond to single agent immunotherapy.
source: Platinum-based chemotherapy is likely to remain an important treatment modality for these patients due to the emergence of resistance to targeted therapies in EGFR, ALK or ROS mutant tumours (Lindeman et al., 2018), and the fact that most patients do not respond to single agent immunotherapy (Kim et al., 2019; Doroshow et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Kim et al., 2019 and Doroshow et al., 2019.

claim: Response rates to platinum-based chemotherapy in lung adenocarcinoma remain below 30% due to the prevalence of innate resistance.
source: Despite the use of platinum-based chemotherapy in lung adenocarcinoma for over four decades, response rates remain below 30% due to the prevalence of innate resistance (Pilkington et al., 2015; Bonanno et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Pilkington et al., 2015 and Bonanno et al., 2014.

claim: Dose-related nephrotoxicity remains a challenge in many patients receiving platinum-based chemotherapy.
source: In addition, dose-related nephrotoxicity remains a challenge in many patients (Pabla and Dong, 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Pabla and Dong, 2008.

claim: Over 147 mechanisms of resistance to platinum chemotherapy have been proposed.
source: However, unravelling platinum resistance in lung adenocarcinoma has proven challenging, as over 147 mechanisms of resistance have been proposed (Stewart, 2007), yet there remains a lack of viable clinical options to improve response rates.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Stewart, 2007.

claim: Both cisplatin and carboplatin are rapidly cleared from the circulation and the tumour within 2–3 hr following administration in humans and rodents.
source: This contrasts with pharmacokinetic studies in humans and rodents demonstrating that both cisplatin and carboplatin are rapidly cleared from the circulation, and the tumour, within 2–3 hr following administration (Andersson et al., 1996; Johansen et al., 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Andersson et al., 1996 and Johansen et al., 2002.

claim: Continuous exposure to cisplatin resulted in decreased cell number and increased apoptosis over 72 hr in A549 cells.
source: This analysis demonstrated that while continuous exposure to cisplatin resulted in decreased cell number and increased apoptosis over 72 hr, a pulse of cisplatin only reduced the rate of cell proliferation and did not induce apoptosis.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from live cell imaging and cell viability assays described in the manuscript.

claim: A pulse of cisplatin only reduced the rate of cell proliferation and did not induce apoptosis in A549 cells.
source: This analysis demonstrated that while continuous exposure to cisplatin resulted in decreased cell number and increased apoptosis over 72 hr, a pulse of cisplatin only reduced the rate of cell proliferation and did not induce apoptosis.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from live cell imaging and cell viability assays described in the manuscript.

claim: The continuous exposure model resulted in a significantly elevated and sustained DNA damage response when compared to the pulse model.
source: As might be expected, the continuous exposure model resulted in a significantly elevated and sustained DNA damage response when compared to the pulse model, particularly for the phosphorylation of Chk2 (Ser345), p53 (Ser15 and Ser46), pH2A.X (Ser139 - γH2A.X) and expression of p21 and MDM2 (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiplexed protein analysis data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: p38 and ERK activation were significantly increased in cells continuously exposed to cisplatin.
source: Furthermore, while p38 and ERK activation were significantly increased in cells continuously exposed to cisplatin, the expression of MCL-1 and detection of MCL-1/Bak dimers only significantly increased in cells treated with a pulse of cisplatin.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiplexed protein analysis data comparing continuous and pulsed cisplatin treatment.

claim: The expression of MCL-1 and detection of MCL-1/Bak dimers only significantly increased in cells treated with a pulse of cisplatin.
source: Furthermore, while p38 and ERK activation were significantly increased in cells continuously exposed to cisplatin, the expression of MCL-1 and detection of MCL-1/Bak dimers only significantly increased in cells treated with a pulse of cisplatin.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiplexed protein analysis data comparing continuous and pulsed cisplatin treatment.

claim: The apoptotic response to cisplatin pulse ranged from ~3% in A549 cells to ~32% in NCI-H1299 cells.
source: Based upon this model we observed a range of sensitivity to cisplatin, from the most resistant A549 line (~3% apoptosis) to the most responsive NCI-H1299 line (~32% apoptosis).
evidence: This claim is supported by apoptosis measurements shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Lung adenocarcinoma cell lines could not be stratified according to their TP53 mutation status based on cisplatin sensitivity.
source: However, these cell lines could not be stratified simply according to their TP53 mutation status, or other frequently observed genetic alterations (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by the apoptosis data across cell lines with different TP53 status shown in Figure 1B.

claim: All six cell lines displayed significant nuclear localised cisplatin-DNA adducts following a 2 hr pulse.
source: This analysis demonstrated that within this model, all six cell lines displayed significant nuclear localised cisplatin-DNA adducts following a 2 hr pulse (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 3), suggesting that drug efflux is not associated with variations in the apoptotic response to a pulse of cisplatin in these lines.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: Drug efflux is not associated with variations in the apoptotic response to a pulse of cisplatin in these cell lines.
source: This analysis demonstrated that within this model, all six cell lines displayed significant nuclear localised cisplatin-DNA adducts following a 2 hr pulse (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 3), suggesting that drug efflux is not associated with variations in the apoptotic response to a pulse of cisplatin in these lines.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that all cell lines showed nuclear cisplatin-DNA adducts despite varying apoptotic responses.

claim: Cisplatin-DNA adducts progressively resolved over a 72 hr period in all cell lines.
source: Furthermore, these cisplatin-DNA adducts progressively resolved over a 72 hr period in all cell lines (Figure 1C), confirming that pathways responsible for facilitating the removal of cisplatin adducts are also functional across this panel.
evidence: This claim is supported by time-course immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Pathways responsible for facilitating the removal of cisplatin adducts are functional across the cell line panel.
source: Furthermore, these cisplatin-DNA adducts progressively resolved over a 72 hr period in all cell lines (Figure 1C), confirming that pathways responsible for facilitating the removal of cisplatin adducts are also functional across this panel.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that cisplatin-DNA adducts resolved over time in all cell lines.

claim: Chk1 (Ser345) phosphorylation increased rapidly in all lines following the 2 hr pulse.
source: In line with the detection of cisplatin-DNA adducts (Figure 1C), Chk1 (Ser345) phosphorylation increased rapidly in all lines following the 2 hr pulse, followed by a slower wave of Chk2 (Thr68) phosphorylation in all lines except SW-1573.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiplexed protein analysis data shown in Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: Chk2 (Thr68) phosphorylation occurred in all lines except SW-1573 following cisplatin pulse.
source: In line with the detection of cisplatin-DNA adducts (Figure 1C), Chk1 (Ser345) phosphorylation increased rapidly in all lines following the 2 hr pulse, followed by a slower wave of Chk2 (Thr68) phosphorylation in all lines except SW-1573.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiplexed protein analysis data shown in Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: In TP53 wildtype cell lines, cisplatin-induced Chk1/Chk2 phosphorylation was followed by p53 phosphorylation and increased expression of MDM2 and p21.
source: Within both the TP53 wildtype cell lines (A549 and SW-1573) this was followed by phosphorylation of p53 (Ser15 and Ser46), the accumulation of total p53 and increased expression of the p53 transcriptional targets MDM2 and p21.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiplexed protein analysis data shown in Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: In TP53 mutant cell lines, p53 phosphorylation occurred but did not result in increased expression of MDM2 or p21.
source: In the TP53 mutant cell lines (NCI-H1573 and NCI-H1975) p53 phosphorylation still occurred, however in line with their loss of DNA binding capability, this did not result in increased expression of MDM2 or p21.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiplexed protein analysis data shown in Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: There was a significant increase in p21 and MDM2 expression in the NCI-H358 line in the absence of p53 expression.
source: Interestingly though, there was a significant increase in p21 and MDM2 expression in the NCI-H358 line in the absence of p53 expression.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiplexed protein analysis data shown in Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: The first four principal components captured ~70% of variance in the dataset.
source: Using this multi-dimensional analysis, we were able to capture ~70% of variance in the dataset within the first four principal components (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by the PCA analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: PC1 and PC2 separated cell lines primarily according to their TP53 status.
source: Unsurprisingly, plotting the first two principal components (PC1 and PC2) against each other (Figure 2A) resulted in separation of the cell lines primarily according to their TP53 status.
evidence: This claim is supported by the PCA plot shown in Figure 2A.

claim: PC3 and PC4 created a clear delineation between the three most resistant cell lines and the three most sensitive lines.
source: However, plotting the third and fourth principal components (PC3 and PC4, Figure 2D,E) created a clear delineation between the three most resistant cell lines (A549, NCI-H358 and NCI-H1573), which cluster towards the left hand side of PC3 (x-axis), and the three most sensitive lines (SW-1573, NCI-1975 and NCI-H1299) which move progressively along PC3 over the 72 hr timeframe.
evidence: This claim is supported by the PCA plot shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Cisplatin sensitive cell lines moved along PC3 towards higher levels of γH2A.X, cleaved caspase 3 and stress-associated MAPK signalling.
source: This is in line with the movement of cisplatin sensitive cell lines along PC3 (x-axis) towards higher levels of γH2A.X (H2A.XS139), cleaved caspase 3 and a stress associated MAPK signalling axis (pATF2, pJNK, pc-Jun) (Figure 2D,E).
evidence: This claim is supported by the PCA plot and analyte distribution shown in Figure 2D and 2E.

claim: Only the inhibition of P70S6K with dactolisib resulted in a significant increase in cisplatin-induced apoptosis in both A549 and NCI-H358 cell lines.
source: Instead, under these conditions, only the inhibition of P70S6K with the dual PI3K/mTOR inhibitor dactolisib resulted in a significant increase in cisplatin-induced apoptosis in both cell lines.
evidence: This claim is supported by apoptosis assay data shown in Figure 3C and 3D.

claim: Specific inhibitors of Akt, STAT3, MEK or NF-κB did not significantly increase apoptosis in A549 or NCI-H358 cell lines.
source: Using the resistant A549 (Figure 3C) and NCI-H358 (Figure 3D) cell lines we observed that specific inhibitors of Akt (MK2206), STAT3 (S3I-201), MEK (UO126) or NF- κB (SC-75741) did not significantly increase apoptosis in either cell line, suggesting that while elevated activity of these signalling proteins may be present in one or both of these resistant lines (Figure 2C), they are not causally associated with resistance to cisplatin.
evidence: This claim is supported by apoptosis assay data shown in Figure 3C and 3D.

claim: The lack of sensitisation by an Akt inhibitor suggests a specific role for P70S6K in mediating resistance to cisplatin.
source: While dactolisib will result in the inhibition of a number of substrates downstream of both PI3K and mTOR, the lack of sensitisation by an Akt inhibitor (MK2206) suggests a specific role for P70S6K in mediating resistance to cisplatin.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the differential effects of dactolisib and Akt inhibitor on cisplatin sensitivity.

claim: Treatment of the resistant NCI-H358 line with dactolisib increased both caspase 3 cleavage and γH2A.X expression to that observed in the sensitive NCI-H1299 line.
source: Crucially, treatment of the resistant NCI-H358 line with dactolisib during and after the cisplatin pulse increased both caspase 3 cleavage and γH2A.X expression to that observed in the sensitive NCI-H1299 line.
evidence: This claim is supported by western blotting data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: P70S6K knockdown with siRNA significantly increased caspase 3 cleavage and γH2A.X expression in cisplatin-treated NCI-H358 cells.
source: Under these conditions, cisplatin treatment resulted in significantly higher caspase 3 cleavage and γH2A.X expression in the P70S6K knockdown NCI-H358 cells (Figure 3G), whilst P70S6K knockdown did not further sensitise the already cisplatin-sensitive NCI-H1299 cell line (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blotting data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: P70S6K knockdown significantly increased cisplatin-induced apoptosis in NCI-H358 cells to the same extent as dactolisib treatment.
source: Additionally, P70S6K knockdown with both siRNAs also significantly increased cisplatin-induced apoptosis in the NCI-H358 cells, to the same extent as that observed with dactolisib treatment (Figure 3H, Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by apoptosis assay data shown in Figure 3H and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The combination of carboplatin and dactolisib completely halted tumour growth in NCI-H358 xenografts up to 28 days following a single pulse of carboplatin treatment.
source: However the combination of carboplatin and dactolisib completely halted tumour growth, even up to 28 days following the single pulse of carboplatin treatment.
evidence: This claim is supported by in vivo xenograft data shown in Figure 3I.

claim: Carboplatin and dactolisib treated xenografts had significantly larger regions of necrosis.
source: Furthermore, an analysis of tumour sections revealed that the carboplatin and dactolisib treated xenografts were not only smaller in size, but also had significantly larger regions of necrosis (Figure 3J).
evidence: This claim is supported by histological analysis data shown in Figure 3J.

claim: RPS6KB1 and RPS6KB2 are amplified or over-expressed in 20% and 11% of lung adenocarcinoma cases, respectively.
source: Indeed, an analysis of TCGA data using cBioPortal (Gao et al., 2013; Cerami et al., 2012; Hoadley et al., 2018) reveals that RPS6KB1 and RPS6KB2, the two isoforms of P70S6K, are amplified or over-expressed in 20% and 11% of lung adenocarcinoma cases, respectively (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by TCGA data analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: TP53 mutations or deletions occur within 47% of lung adenocarcinomas.
source: Importantly, while TP53 mutations or deletions also occur within 47% of lung adenocarcinomas, RPS6KB1 and RPS6KB2 amplification/over-expression occur on the background of either wildtype or mutant TP53.
evidence: This claim is supported by TCGA data analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Elevated mRNA expression of both RPS6KB1 and RPS6KB2 isoforms was significantly associated with poor overall survival of lung adenocarcinoma patients.
source: Further analysis with KM plotter (Győrffy et al., 2013) demonstrated that the elevated mRNA expression of both isoforms was also significantly associated with poor overall survival of lung adenocarcinoma patients (Figure 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by survival analysis data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: High expression of P70S6K was significantly associated with poor overall survival in a cohort of 52 lung adenocarcinoma patients.
source: In this cohort, high expression of P70S6K was significantly associated with poor overall survival (Figure 4D), while there was a non-significant trend towards higher P70S6K expression in patients with progressive disease (Figure 4E) and a later disease stage (Figure 4F).
evidence: This claim is supported by IHC and survival analysis data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: P70S6K expression was significantly increased upon relapse in eight patients with matched diagnosis and relapse samples.
source: In eight patients with matched diagnosis and relapse samples, the levels of P70S6K expression were also significantly increased upon relapse (Figure 4G), further highlighting the functional role of P70S6K in the cellular response to platinum therapy.
evidence: This claim is supported by IHC analysis of matched patient samples shown in Figure 4G.

claim: Treatment with a single pulse of cisplatin caused A549 and NCI-H358 cells to be significantly more likely to remain arrested in G1.
source: First, A549 (TP53 wildtype) and NCI-H358 (TP53 null) cells were significantly more likely to remain arrested in G1, both before (G1 arrest before mitosis; ABM) and after undergoing mitosis (G1 arrest after mitosis; AAM) (Figure 5B,C).
evidence: This claim is supported by FUCCI live-cell imaging data shown in Figure 5B and 5C.

claim: NCI-H1573 cells did not show any significant increase in G1 transit time following cisplatin treatment.
source: In contrast, NCI-H1573 cells did not show any significant increase in G1 transit time, as may be expected from a TP53 mutant cell line.
evidence: This claim is supported by FUCCI live-cell imaging data shown in Figure 5B and 5C.

claim: Cisplatin pulsing resulted in a significant increase in S/G2 transit time for all cell lines.
source: For all cell lines, cisplatin pulsing resulted in a significant increase in S/G2 transit time (Figure 5B,C).
evidence: This claim is supported by FUCCI live-cell imaging data shown in Figure 5B and 5C.

claim: NCI-H1573 and NCI-H358 cells delayed for more time in G2 compared to A549 cells after cisplatin treatment.
source: Notably, the NCI-H1573 (TP53 mutant) and NCI-H358 (TP53 null) cells delayed for more time in G2 (G2 arrest; mean 2443 min and 2555 min respectively) compared to A549 cells (mean 1426 min), after which the mutant and null cells often entered a prolonged aberrant mitosis (Figure 5—figure supplement 1), resulting in a small increase in cells dying during mitosis or in the following G1/S phase (Figure 5C, death after mitosis; DAM).
evidence: This claim is supported by FUCCI live-cell imaging data shown in Figure 5B, 5C, and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Many cisplatin-treated A549 cells turned from green (S/G2) back to red (G1) without undergoing mitosis (G2-exit).
source: In contrast, A549 cells rarely entered into mitosis, instead many of these S/G2 arrested cells turned from green (S/G2) back to red (G1) without undergoing mitosis (G2-exit) (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by FUCCI live-cell imaging data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: siRNA-mediated knockdown of p53 in A549 cells resulted in a significant increase in G2-arrest and a decrease in G2-exit.
source: In line with this hypothesis, this orthogonal approach revealed a significant increase in G2-arrest in the p53 knockdown cells, along with a decrease in occurrence of G2-exit, effectively pheno-copying the observed difference between the A549 wildtype and NCI-H358 p53 null cell lines (Figure 5C).
evidence: This claim is supported by FUCCI live-cell imaging data with p53 knockdown shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: Treatment of all cell lines with dactolisib as a single agent caused a significant increase in G1 arrest both before and after mitosis, irrespective of TP53 status.
source: Treatment of all cell lines with dactolisib as a single agent also caused a significant increase in G1 arrest both before (G1 ABM) and after mitosis (G1 AAM), irrespective of TP53 status (Figure 5B,C).
evidence: This claim is supported by FUCCI live-cell imaging data shown in Figure 5B and 5C.

claim: For TP53 wildtype and null cells in late G1 or S phase at the time of cisplatin pulsing, dactolisib treatment significantly reduced S/G2 transit time and greatly increased apoptosis before mitosis.
source: However, for the TP53 wildtype and null cells that were in late G1 or S phase at the time of cisplatin pulsing, dactolisib treatment significantly reduced S/G2 transit time (Figure 5B) and greatly increased the number of cells that underwent apoptosis before mitosis (Death before mitosis; DBM) (Figure 5C,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by FUCCI live-cell imaging data shown in Figure 5B, 5C, and 5D.

claim: Dactolisib treatment significantly increased the duration of mitotic arrest, independent of TP53 status.
source: Notably, dactolisib treatment did not prevent cisplatin treated cells from entering into an aberrant mitosis, but did significantly increase the duration of mitotic arrest, independent of TP53 status (Figure 5B), which correlated with an increase in death during or after mitosis (DAM) in TP53 wildtype and null, but not mutant cells (Figure 5C,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by FUCCI live-cell imaging data shown in Figure 5B, 5C, and 5D.

claim: Dactolisib treatment did not result in any sensitisation of TP53 mutant H1573 cells to cisplatin.
source: Surprisingly, dactolisib treatment did not result in any sensitisation of TP53 mutant H1573 cells to cisplatin (Figure 5D), which also corresponded with a failure of dactolisib to significantly reduce S/G2 phase transit time (Figure 5B).
evidence: This claim is supported by FUCCI live-cell imaging data shown in Figure 5B and 5D.

claim: siRNA-mediated P70S6K knockdown in NCI-H358 cells resulted in a non-significant trend towards a shortened G2-arrest and greatly increased cell death both before or after mitosis.
source: This approach demonstrated that specific ablation of P70S6K in this model resulted in a non-significant trend towards a shortened G2-arrest with both P70S6K siRNAs, and a greatly increased cell death both before (DBM) or after mitosis (DAM).
evidence: This claim is supported by FUCCI live-cell imaging data with P70S6K knockdown shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3.

claim: There was increased expression of p21 following cisplatin treatment in the resistant NCI-H358 line, but not the sensitive NCI-H1299 line.
source: While both the NCI-H1299 and NCI-H358 cell lines are TP53 null, there was an increased expression of p21 following cisplatin treatment in the resistant NCI-H358 line, but not the sensitive NCI-H1299 line.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiplexed protein analysis data shown in Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: The increased p21 expression by NCI-H358 cells was efficiently inhibited by both treatment with dactolisib and the specific knockdown of P70S6K with siRNA.
source: Importantly, the increased p21 expression by NCI-H358 cells was also observed by western blotting of independent samples and was efficiently inhibited by both treatment with dactolisib (Figure 6A,B) and the specific knockdown of P70S6K with siRNA (Figure 6C).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blotting data shown in Figure 6A, 6B, and 6C.

claim: p63 is elevated in the NCI-H358 line following treatment with cisplatin, and is inhibited by the addition of dactolisib or treatment with P70S6K siRNA.
source: However, in the absence of p53, we observed that this may potentially be mediated by the related transcription factor p63, which is elevated in the NCI-H358 line following treatment with cisplatin, and also inhibited by the addition of dactolisib (Figure 6A,B) or treatment with P70S6K siRNA (Figure 6C).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blotting data shown in Figure 6A, 6B, and 6C.

claim: Both TP53 wildtype cell lines were significantly sensitised to cisplatin by the addition of dactolisib.
source: In accordance with this hypothesis, and in line with the FUCCI single-cell imaging (Figure 5A), both the TP53 wildtype cell lines were significantly sensitised to cisplatin by the addition dactolisib, as was the resistant TP53 null line, NCI-H358 (Figures 2D, H and 6D).
evidence: This claim is supported by apoptosis assay data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: The resistant TP53 null line, NCI-H358, was significantly sensitised to cisplatin by the addition of dactolisib.
source: In accordance with this hypothesis, and in line with the FUCCI single-cell imaging (Figure 5A), both the TP53 wildtype cell lines were significantly sensitised to cisplatin by the addition dactolisib, as was the resistant TP53 null line, NCI-H358 (Figures 2D, H and 6D).
evidence: This claim is supported by apoptosis assay data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Dactolisib was not able to increase cisplatin-induced apoptosis in the TP53 mutant line NCI-H1573.
source: Also, in line with the FUCCI analysis, dactolisib was not able to increase cisplatin-induced apoptosis in the TP53 mutant line NCI-H1573, whilst it significantly antagonised cisplatin-induced apoptosis in the TP53 mutant NCI-H1975 line.
evidence: This claim is supported by apoptosis assay data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Dactolisib significantly antagonised cisplatin-induced apoptosis in the TP53 mutant NCI-H1975 line.
source: Also, in line with the FUCCI analysis, dactolisib was not able to increase cisplatin-induced apoptosis in the TP53 mutant line NCI-H1573, whilst it significantly antagonised cisplatin-induced apoptosis in the TP53 mutant NCI-H1975 line.
evidence: This claim is supported by apoptosis assay data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: The addition of dactolisib to the TP53 wildtype A549 cell line inhibited cisplatin-induced p53 and p21 accumulation, resulting in elevated markers of DNA damage and apoptosis.
source: In line with this hypothesis, the addition of dactolisib to the TP53 wildtype A549 cell line inhibited cisplatin-induced p53 and p21 accumulation, resulting in elevated markers of DNA damage (γH2A.X expression) and apoptosis (caspase 3 cleavage) following cisplatin treatment (Figure 6E).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blotting data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: In the TP53 mutant NCI-H1573 line, p21 expression was not significantly elevated following cisplatin treatment, and γH2A.X expression and caspase 3 cleavage were unchanged by the addition of dactolisib.
source: However, in the TP53 mutant NCI-H1573 line, which was not sensitised by dactolisib, p21 expression was not significantly elevated following cisplatin treatment, and γH2A.X expression and caspase 3 cleavage were unchanged by the addition of dactolisib (Figure 7).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blotting data shown in Figure 6E (referenced as Figure 7 in the text).

claim: A strong correlation was observed between phosphorylated P70S6K levels and decreased apoptosis in response to cisplatin for wildtype TP53 lines (r2 = 0.6092).
source: However, the strength of this correlation was greatly increased when considering the TP53 status of the lines, with a strong correlation observed for wildtype TP53 lines (r2 = 0.6092) but no correlation for TP53 mutant lines (r2 = 0.1764).
evidence: This claim is supported by correlation analysis data shown in Figure 6G.

claim: No correlation was observed between phosphorylated P70S6K levels and apoptosis in response to cisplatin for TP53 mutant lines (r2 = 0.1764).
source: However, the strength of this correlation was greatly increased when considering the TP53 status of the lines, with a strong correlation observed for wildtype TP53 lines (r2 = 0.6092) but no correlation for TP53 mutant lines (r2 = 0.1764).
evidence: This claim is supported by correlation analysis data shown in Figure 6G.

claim: Combination therapy with cisplatin and dactolisib significantly sensitised the high pP70S6K/TP53 wildtype NCI-H292 cell line.
source: In agreement with our finding that elevated P70S6K activity promotes resistance in a TP53 dependent manner, combination therapy with cisplatin and dactolisib significantly sensitised the high pP70S6K/TP53 wildtype NCI-H292 cell line, but not the high pP70S6K/TP53 mutant NCI-H2009 line.
evidence: This claim is supported by apoptosis assay data shown in Figure 6H.

claim: Combination therapy with cisplatin and dactolisib did not sensitise the high pP70S6K/TP53 mutant NCI-H2009 line.
source: In agreement with our finding that elevated P70S6K activity promotes resistance in a TP53 dependent manner, combination therapy with cisplatin and dactolisib significantly sensitised the high pP70S6K/TP53 wildtype NCI-H292 cell line, but not the high pP70S6K/TP53 mutant NCI-H2009 line.
evidence: This claim is supported by apoptosis assay data shown in Figure 6H.

claim: P70S6K promotes an aberrant G2-exit or prolonged G2-arrest following cisplatin treatment through enhanced translation of p53/p21 in TP53 wildtype cell lines and p63/p21 in TP53 null lines.
source: Therefore, this data demonstrates that P70S6K promotes an aberrant G2-exit or prolonged G2-arrest following cisplatin treatment, presumably through enhanced translation of p53/p21 in TP53 wildtype cell lines and p63/p21 in TP53 null lines (Figure 7).
evidence: This claim is inferred from the combined data on P70S6K effects on cell cycle, p21 expression, and TP53 status-dependent responses.

claim: In the presence of mutant p53, P70S6K is not able to influence the DNA damage induced signalling axis and is therefore not associated with sensitivity to cisplatin.
source: However, in the presence of mutant p53, P70S6K is not able to influence this DNA damage induced signalling axis and is therefore not associated with sensitivity to cisplatin.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that dactolisib does not sensitize TP53 mutant cells to cisplatin.

claim: Continuous culturing of cells in the presence of high doses of platinum drugs in vitro would result in the accumulation of numerous off-target adducts and the activation of a stress response incongruent with the actual in vivo apoptotic mechanism.
source: It is likely that the continuous culturing of cells in the presence of high doses of these drugs in vitro would result in the accumulation of numerous off-target adducts and the activation of a stress response incongruent with the actual in vivo apoptotic mechanism.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the comparison of continuous and pulsed cisplatin treatment models.

claim: p38 activity is induced by the continuous exposure model, but not by the pulse model.
source: Indeed, this effect may be apparent in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D/2, where p38 activity is induced by the continuous exposure model, but not by the pulse model.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiplexed protein analysis data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Highly elevated p38 signalling was not observed in any cell line following the cisplatin pulse.
source: A number of previous studies have implicated the activity of p38 in mediating resistance to cisplatin (Sarin et al., 2018; Pereira et al., 2013; Galan-Moya et al., 2011; Hernández Losa et al., 2003), however we did not observe highly elevated p38 signalling in any cell line following the cisplatin pulse (Figure 1D), nor a correlation between p38 activity and the apoptotic response (Figure 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiplexed protein analysis data shown in Figure 1D and the PCA analysis in Figure 2.

claim: High levels of P70S6K expression have previously been associated with aggressive tumour behaviour in lung cancer.
source: High levels of P70S6K expression have previously been associated with aggressive tumour behaviour in lung cancer (Chen et al., 2017), as well as other cancer types such as breast (Holz, 2012), colorectal (Nozawa et al., 2007) and liver (Sahin et al., 2004) cancers.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Chen et al., 2017, Holz, 2012, Nozawa et al., 2007, and Sahin et al., 2004.

claim: P70S6K can regulate cell cycle progression via the enhanced translation of p21 mRNA.
source: Further supporting this central role of P70S6K, previous research has demonstrated that P70S6K can regulate cell cycle progression via the enhanced translation of p21 mRNA (Guégan et al., 2014), although our data also suggest that P70S6K may also play a role in the enhanced expression of both p53 and p63 in this context.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Guégan et al., 2014.

claim: The combination of cisplatin and dactolisib has previously been proposed for osteosarcoma, head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, and bladder cancer.
source: The combination of cisplatin and dactolisib has also previously been proposed for osteosarcoma (Huang et al., 2018), head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (Hsu et al., 2018) and bladder cancer (Moon et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Huang et al., 2018, Hsu et al., 2018, and Moon et al., 2014.

claim: The failure of many clinical trials is frequently attributed to the lack of suitable biomarkers to stratify the patient cohort.
source: This fine grained stratification of response is an important finding, as the failure of many clinical trials is frequently attributed to the lack of suitable biomarkers to stratify the patient cohort (Hay et al., 2014), highlighting the value of our approach that is capable of dissecting the mechanism of variable drug response across differing genetic backgrounds.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Hay et al., 2014.

claim: The inability of dactolisib to regulate p21 expression in TP53 mutant tumour cells following cisplatin treatment likely underlies the inability of dactolisib to sensitise these cells to cisplatin.
source: The inability of dactolisib to regulate p21 expression in TP53 mutant tumour cells following cisplatin treatment likely underlies the inability of dactolisib to sensitise these cells to cisplatin.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the combined observations of p21 regulation and sensitization patterns across different TP53 backgrounds.

claim: Within the context of a potential clinical trial for cisplatin and dactolisib combination, the TP53 mutation status of each patient tumour would be a central consideration for identification of the most effective treatment strategy.
source: Therefore, within the context of a potential clinical trial for this drug combination, the TP53 mutation status of each patient tumour would be a central consideration for identification of the most effective treatment strategy and an understanding of individual patient response.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the TP53-dependent effects of dactolisib on cisplatin sensitivity.

claim: Platinum therapies work by forming covalent DNA adducts, which distort the DNA helix and block replication.
source: As platinum chemotherapies work by forming covalent DNA adducts, which distort the DNA helix and block replication, the progressive accumulation of single stranded and double stranded breaks is thought to induce apoptosis (Jamieson and Lippard, 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Jamieson and Lippard, 1999.

claim: The progressive accumulation of single stranded and double stranded breaks is thought to induce apoptosis following platinum chemotherapy.
source: As platinum chemotherapies work by forming covalent DNA adducts, which distort the DNA helix and block replication, the progressive accumulation of single stranded and double stranded breaks is thought to induce apoptosis (Jamieson and Lippard, 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Jamieson and Lippard, 1999.

claim: A G2-exit, senescence state has been reported to be dependent on p21.
source: A similar G2-exit, senescence state has been reported to be dependent on p21 (Gire and Dulic, 2015) and likely provides TP53 wildtype cells protection from death by preventing progression through an aberrant mitosis.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Gire and Dulic, 2015.

claim: G2-exit likely provides TP53 wildtype cells protection from death by preventing progression through an aberrant mitosis.
source: A similar G2-exit, senescence state has been reported to be dependent on p21 (Gire and Dulic, 2015) and likely provides TP53 wildtype cells protection from death by preventing progression through an aberrant mitosis.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation of G2-exit in TP53 wildtype cells and its association with reduced apoptosis.

claim: In TP53 wildtype A549 cells, dactolisib induced pre-mitotic cell death and prevented cells from undergoing a protective G2-exit.
source: In the TP53 wildtype A549 cells it induced pre-mitotic cell death and prevented cells from undergoing a protective G2-exit, which is likely partially dependent on the p53-p21 axis.
evidence: This claim is supported by FUCCI live-cell imaging data shown in Figure 5.

claim: In the TP53 null NCI-H358 line, dactolisib promoted both pre-mitotic cell death and the entry of cells into a prolonged deleterious aberrant mitosis.
source: Similarly, in the TP53 null line, dactolisib promoted both pre-mitotic cell death and the entry of cells into a prolonged deleterious aberrant mitosis, the latter likely due to a weakened p53-dependent G2 checkpoint (Engeland, 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by FUCCI live-cell imaging data shown in Figure 5.

claim: In TP53 mutant H1573 cells, there was no significant sensitisation by dactolisib due to a sustained S/G2 arrest in the presence of dactolisib.
source: While in TP53 mutant H1573 cells, there was no significant sensitisation due to a sustained S/G2 arrest in the presence of dactolisib.
evidence: This claim is supported by FUCCI live-cell imaging data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Dactolisib treatment of cells within early G1 phase during the cisplatin pulse resulted in many cells remaining arrested and viable in G1, highlighting the importance of DNA replication for inducing cisplatin induced toxicity and killing.
source: Consequently, for all cell lines, dactolisib treatment of cells within early G1 phase during the cisplatin pulse resulted in many cells remaining arrested and viable in G1 (G1 ABM), highlighting the importance of DNA replication for inducing cisplatin induced toxicity and killing.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the FUCCI live-cell imaging data showing G1 arrest and reduced apoptosis.

claim: The cisplatin pulse model more closely recapitulates physiological pharmacokinetics compared to continuous exposure models.
source: Therefore, in this study we have utilised a cisplatin pulse model, which more closely recapitulates these physiological pharmacokinetics, aiming to maintain the fidelity of the apoptotic mechanism mediated by cisplatin in vivo.
evidence: This claim is based on pharmacokinetic studies cited in the manuscript (Andersson et al., 1996; Johansen et al., 2002).

claim: Predictive computational models of drug-induced apoptotic signalling dynamics can be used as a prognostic indicator of neuroblastoma patient survival.
source: We have previously shown that predictive computational models of drug-induced apoptotic signalling dynamics can be used as a prognostic indicator of neuroblastoma patient survival (Fey et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Fey et al., 2015.

claim: Elevated P70S6K activity is frequently observed in several cancer subtypes, including lung cancer.
source: Importantly, elevated P70S6K activity is frequently observed in several cancer subtypes, including lung cancer (Chen et al., 2017), and its overexpression is commonly associated with aggressive malignant phenotypes and poor overall prognoses (Ip and Wong, 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Chen et al., 2017 and Ip and Wong, 2012.

claim: P70S6K overexpression is commonly associated with aggressive malignant phenotypes and poor overall prognoses.
source: Importantly, elevated P70S6K activity is frequently observed in several cancer subtypes, including lung cancer (Chen et al., 2017), and its overexpression is commonly associated with aggressive malignant phenotypes and poor overall prognoses (Ip and Wong, 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Ip and Wong, 2012.

claim: RPS6KB1 and RPS6KB2 amplification/over-expression occur on the background of either wildtype or mutant TP53.
source: Importantly, while TP53 mutations or deletions also occur within 47% of lung adenocarcinomas, RPS6KB1 and RPS6KB2 amplification/over-expression occur on the background of either wildtype or mutant TP53.
evidence: This claim is supported by TCGA data analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: P70S6K is a serine/threonine-specific protein kinase known to require phosphorylation by both PI3K and mTOR for activation.
source: P70S6K is a serine/threonine-specific protein kinase known to require phosphorylation by both PI3K and mTOR for activation (Sunami et al., 2010; Moser et al., 1997).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Sunami et al., 2010 and Moser et al., 1997.

claim: Carboplatin had no significant effect upon tumour growth in NCI-H358 xenografts as a single agent.
source: Under these conditions, carboplatin had no significant effect upon tumour growth, while dactolisib had a moderate effect as a single agent that was only significant at days 14 and 17.
evidence: This claim is supported by in vivo xenograft data shown in Figure 3I.

claim: Dactolisib had a moderate effect on tumour growth as a single agent that was only significant at days 14 and 17 in NCI-H358 xenografts.
source: Under these conditions, carboplatin had no significant effect upon tumour growth, while dactolisib had a moderate effect as a single agent that was only significant at days 14 and 17.
evidence: This claim is supported by in vivo xenograft data shown in Figure 3I.

claim: The inclusion of a JNK inhibitor did not prevent cisplatin induced apoptosis in the SW-1573 cell line.
source: However, the inclusion of a JNK inhibitor (JNK inhibitor VIII) did not prevent cisplatin induced apoptosis in this cell line (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C), suggesting that JNK activity was not promoting apoptosis in this context.
evidence: This claim is supported by apoptosis assay data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: JNK activity was not promoting apoptosis in the SW-1573 cell line following cisplatin treatment.
source: However, the inclusion of a JNK inhibitor (JNK inhibitor VIII) did not prevent cisplatin induced apoptosis in this cell line (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C), suggesting that JNK activity was not promoting apoptosis in this context.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that JNK inhibition did not prevent apoptosis.
